subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Puberty: Tanner stages, precocious and delayed puberty
vignette: A pediatrician is assessing a group of school-age children for normal pubertal development. She uses sexual maturity rating (Tanner staging), which is assigned independently to genitalia, pubic hair, and breast. She wants to identify the first sign of puberty in a boy.
question: Which of the following is the earliest detectable secondary sexual characteristic in males?
explanation_correct: The earliest detectable secondary sexual characteristic in males is testicular enlargement (increased testicular volume, often defined as greater than 4 mL or 2.5 cm). In females the earliest sign is breast bud development (thelarche). Tanner stage 2 marks the onset of puberty with testicular enlargement in boys and breast budding in girls.

explanation_incorrect.A: Pubarche (pubic hair) usually appears after the first sign; testicular enlargement precedes it in boys.
explanation_incorrect.B: Penile lengthening occurs later in puberty (around stage 3), after testicular enlargement.
explanation_incorrect.C: Voice deepening is a later pubertal change driven by testosterone, not the first sign.
explanation_incorrect.D: The growth spurt occurs later in puberty and is not the earliest detectable sign.

educationalObjective: Identify testicular enlargement as the earliest sign of male puberty and breast budding (thelarche) as the earliest in females.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Puberty: Tanner stages, precocious and delayed puberty
vignette: A 13-year-old girl is examined for pubertal staging. She has coarse pubic hair spread across the pubis but sparing the thighs. Her breasts show enlargement with the areola elevated as a separate mound above the breast mound. There is no hair on the medial thighs.
question: Which Tanner stage of breast development is described by a raised areola forming a 'mound on a mound'?
explanation_correct: In Tanner stage IV, the breast enlarges further and the areola elevates to form a secondary mound above the level of the breast (a 'mound on a mound'), and pubic hair is coarse but spares the thighs. Stage V is the adult contour, in which the areola flattens and hair extends to the medial thigh. This patient's findings are classic stage IV.

explanation_incorrect.B: Stage II is the breast bud (thelarche) with a flat-appearing chest and raised nipple, not a mound on a mound.
explanation_incorrect.C: Stage III shows breast enlargement with coarse pubic hair but no separate areolar mound.
explanation_incorrect.D: Stage V is the adult breast contour with a flattened areola and hair extending to the medial thigh, which this patient does not have.
explanation_incorrect.E: Stage I is prepubertal with no sexual hair and no breast development.

educationalObjective: Recognize Tanner stage IV breast development (mound on a mound) and its associated pubic hair pattern.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Puberty: Tanner stages, precocious and delayed puberty
vignette: A 7-year-old girl is brought in for breast buds and pubic hair that appeared over the past year. Bone age is advanced. Laboratory testing shows elevated LH and FSH that respond to GnRH stimulation, and pelvic ultrasound is normal without an ovarian mass.
question: Which of the following best characterizes the most common form of precocious puberty in this patient?

options.text: Peripheral precocious puberty from an estrogen-secreting granulosa cell tumor
McCune-Albright syndrome with GnRH-independent estrogen production
Congenital adrenal hyperplasia causing androgen excess
A Leydig cell tumor secreting testosterone

explanation_correct: Precocious puberty is the appearance of secondary sexual characteristics before age 8 in females and age 9 in males. Central (GnRH-dependent) precocious puberty is the most common form and is usually idiopathic, reflecting early activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis; CNS tumors are another cause. The elevated, GnRH-responsive LH/FSH and absence of a tumor support this diagnosis.

explanation_incorrect.A: A granulosa cell tumor causes peripheral (GnRH-independent) precocious puberty with suppressed LH/FSH and would be visible as an ovarian mass.
explanation_incorrect.B: McCune-Albright syndrome is a peripheral, GnRH-independent cause and would not show elevated GnRH-responsive LH/FSH.
explanation_incorrect.D: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia is a peripheral cause of precocious puberty via adrenal androgen excess, not the most common central form.
explanation_incorrect.E: A Leydig cell tumor is a peripheral cause seen in males, not in a female, and would suppress gonadotropins.

educationalObjective: Distinguish central (GnRH-dependent, idiopathic, most common) from peripheral precocious puberty.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Puberty: Tanner stages, precocious and delayed puberty
vignette: A 15-year-old male has not developed any secondary sexual characteristics. He is tall with gynecomastia and has small, firm testes. Laboratory studies show markedly elevated LH and FSH with a low testosterone level. A buccal smear reveals a Barr body.
question: Which of the following best categorizes the mechanism of his delayed puberty?

options.text: Hypogonadotropic (secondary) hypogonadism due to Kallmann syndrome
Hypergonadotropic (primary) hypogonadism due to Klinefelter syndrome
Constitutional delay of growth and puberty (late blooming)
Hypogonadotropic (secondary) hypogonadism due to a CNS lesion
Hypergonadotropic (primary) hypogonadism due to Turner syndrome

explanation_correct: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) is a cause of hypergonadotropic (primary) hypogonadism and is one of the listed causes of delayed puberty. Gonadal failure leads to low testosterone with loss of negative feedback, so LH and FSH are elevated. The tall stature, gynecomastia, small firm testes, and Barr body (from the extra X) are classic. Delayed puberty is defined as absence of secondary sexual characteristics by age 14 in males.

explanation_incorrect.A: Kallmann syndrome causes hypogonadotropic (secondary) hypogonadism with low LH/FSH and is associated with anosmia, not elevated gonadotropins.
explanation_incorrect.C: Constitutional delay is hypogonadotropic and a diagnosis of exclusion with normal gonadotropins for bone age; it would not cause small firm testes or a Barr body.
explanation_incorrect.D: A CNS lesion would cause hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with low LH/FSH, not the elevated levels seen here.
explanation_incorrect.E: Turner syndrome (45,X) is a cause of hypergonadotropic hypogonadism but occurs in females, not males.

educationalObjective: Classify Klinefelter syndrome as a cause of hypergonadotropic (primary) delayed puberty with elevated LH/FSH.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Puberty: Tanner stages, precocious and delayed puberty
vignette: A 6-year-old girl presents with breast development and pubic hair. She also has irregular cafe-au-lait skin patches and bone lesions consistent with fibrous dysplasia. Hormone studies show elevated estrogen with suppressed LH and FSH that do not respond to GnRH stimulation.
question: Which of the following mechanisms best explains this patient's precocious puberty?

options.text: Increased GnRH secretion from early activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis
A CNS tumor driving excess GnRH release
Idiopathic central precocious puberty with increased LH and FSH
GnRH-independent sex hormone production (peripheral precocious puberty)
Failure of epiphyseal plate closure from estrogen deficiency

explanation_correct: McCune-Albright syndrome causes peripheral (GnRH-independent) precocious puberty through autonomous sex hormone production, and is classically associated with cafe-au-lait spots and fibrous dysplasia. The suppressed LH/FSH that fail to respond to GnRH confirm a GnRH-independent mechanism, distinguishing it from central precocious puberty. Other peripheral causes include congenital adrenal hyperplasia, granulosa cell tumors, and Leydig cell tumors.

explanation_incorrect.A: Increased GnRH secretion is the mechanism of central precocious puberty, which would show elevated, GnRH-responsive LH/FSH, not suppressed levels.
explanation_incorrect.B: A GnRH-secreting CNS tumor is a central cause and would not produce suppressed LH/FSH or the cafe-au-lait/fibrous dysplasia findings.
explanation_incorrect.C: Idiopathic central precocious puberty is GnRH-dependent and is the most common overall cause, but it does not fit the suppressed gonadotropins or this syndrome's stigmata.
explanation_incorrect.E: Estrogen deficiency would delay puberty and keep epiphyses open; here there is excess estrogen with accelerated skeletal maturation.

educationalObjective: Recognize McCune-Albright syndrome as a peripheral (GnRH-independent) cause of precocious puberty with suppressed gonadotropins.

subject: Reproductive
subtopic: Puberty: Tanner stages, precocious and delayed puberty
vignette: A 16-year-old male is evaluated for absence of secondary sexual characteristics. He has never developed pubic hair or testicular enlargement and has no sense of smell. Laboratory studies show low LH, low FSH, and low testosterone.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Kallmann syndrome is hypogonadotropic (secondary) hypogonadism caused by deficient GnRH secretion, and it is classically associated with anosmia (absent sense of smell). The low LH, FSH, and testosterone with delayed secondary sexual characteristics fit this diagnosis. It is a classic cause of delayed puberty in the hypogonadotropic category, alongside constitutional delay and CNS lesions.

explanation_incorrect.B: Klinefelter syndrome causes hypergonadotropic hypogonadism with elevated LH/FSH and small firm testes, not low gonadotropins and anosmia.
explanation_incorrect.C: Turner syndrome occurs in females and causes hypergonadotropic hypogonadism with elevated gonadotropins.
explanation_incorrect.D: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia is a cause of precocious puberty (peripheral) via androgen excess, not hypogonadotropic delayed puberty.
explanation_incorrect.E: A granulosa cell tumor secretes estrogen and causes peripheral precocious puberty in females, not delayed puberty in a male.

educationalObjective: Identify Kallmann syndrome as hypogonadotropic delayed puberty associated with anosmia and low LH/FSH/testosterone.
